summary: This bill prohibits health plans and insurers from applying deductibles to epinephrine delivery systems and caps patient cost-sharing at $60 per package of two systems, effective for plan years beginning on or after January 1, 2026.

scores.thoughts: This bill directly mandates that health plans cover epinephrine delivery systems without deductibles and with limited cost-sharing. This increases access to a specific medical device, which is a move towards more public healthcare access through regulation of private plans.

The bill's sole purpose is to mandate that group and individual health plans cover epinephrine delivery systems with no deductible and cost-sharing capped at $60 per package. This is direct government intervention to reduce consumer out-of-pocket costs for a specific class of medical products.
